comments.body: I found it to be pretty good at structural rigid things like this, guns, buildings etc. But not so great at organic things like plants. Did you give it a reference image first? That seems to really speed things up with better end product.

replies.author: ElwinLewis
replies.body: Building a StarDiabloDew and can confirm, my buildings for the town are really starting to make me happy. It knows about architecture and seems to have no trouble iterating into a nice looking (to my eyes) building (s)

replies.author: CryoNigiri_
replies.body: Yeah, I probably should’ve just given it reference images from the start. At the very end, it kept making the windshield rounded, and no matter how many times I told it to make it square, it wouldn’t listen. I finally showed it a picture and was like “THIS is what I mean,” and then it finally fixed it 😂

comments.author: Interesting-Bee-113
comments.body:
I spend so so so much time trying to get Opus to model a rally car for me.

It was pretty bad and never once could we reliably make any directed corrections

I ended up deciding that actually modeling it by hand would be better and faster some how.

replies.author: CryoNigiri_
replies.body: Yeah, exactly. It used to be basically useless for this. Opus 5 seems way better at spatial reasoning though, and that’s what really surprised me this time.

replies.body: No rig this time since it’s a mechanical model. I figured I could just animate the moving parts directly in Unity, so I had it make the propeller, control stick, and doors as separate pieces.
